title: Telemedical centre for out-of-hospital ventilation and oxygen therapy
summary:
The number of patients who are ventilated at home has been increasing for years. Due to the many concomitant illnesses that patients often suffer from, care by GPs close to home is not sufficient and the quality of care is inadequate due to long and costly journeys to a specialist centre and months of waiting times. Normally, home ventilation checks should be carried out during a hospital stay; outpatient checks by specialised outpatient clinics (e.g. the CABS at Charité-Universitätsmedizin Berlin) are only possible at selected hospitals. The new form of treatment investigated in T-CABS involves recording digital health data from home (telemedicine), which is adapted to the requirements of patients with home ventilation. These data are automatically transmitted to the study team. Scheduled check-up appointments with physical patient presence are to be replaced by video consultations and the telemedical connection will enable early detection of clinical changes in condition that require intervention. Therapy devices (telemetry, telemonitoring) will be connected to the possibilities of digital consultations (e.g. video consultations).  
Study inclusion and completion will take place on site in both groups. The duration for the individual patients is 12 months in each case.
conditions: Spinal muscular atrophy and related syndromes
Myasthenia gravis and other myoneural disorders
Other degenerative diseases of nervous system, not elsewhere classified

interventions.name: Intervention group: Receives telemedical care. Therefore, on-site visits are replaced by video consultations. Additionally, there will be a weekly telemedical check of health data.
Control group: Does not receive telemedical care but continues to come to the outpatient clinic for on-site visits.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Indication for invasive or non-invasive ventilation 
- Chronic ventilatory insufficiency with or without long-term oxygen therapy 
- Written consent to participate in the study 
- Ventilation using a cloud-capable device from the manufacturers BREAS Medical, Löwenstein Medical or ResMed 
- Sufficient experience in handling technical devices by the patient or carer/relatives 
- Majority (age ≥18 years at the time of inclusion)
Exclusion criteria:
- Participation in another telemedical intervention study 
- Acute ventilatory failure with indication for short-term NIV/IV 
- Ascertained pregnancy 
- Evidence of acute or persistent suicidal behaviour 
- Diagnosed advanced dementia 
- Diagnosed advanced tumour disease 
- Minor (<18 years) 
- Planned relocation outside the Berlin/Brandenburg region within the next 12 months
